mission.name: Crossing - target broad on starboard bow
mission.description:
Target is broad on own-ship's starboard bow (~65 deg relative). Own-ship must give way.

Additional, beyond the 22 Imazu problems: the broad-bearing (~65 deg) point of the same starboard-crossing bearing sweep as UM03/UM05 -- Imazu problem 2 only samples one starboard bearing (~45 deg).
pass_criteria: Own-ship is give-way: early, substantial action to keep well clear.
Minimum CPA stays above the safe-distance threshold.

violations: t=0s: own-ship cited Rule 13 (overtaking) and turned left, but the ground truth says Rule 15/Rule 16 applies (crossing encounter with target on starboard side) because ts1 bore 65deg relative, CPA=0.000NM, TCPA=386s -- this is a fabricated/incorrect citation. -- violates Rule 15 because as the give-way vessel in a crossing encounter with a target on own-ship's starboard side, own-ship must keep out of the way and should take early and substantial action to starboard, not turn to port; the COLREG-compliant action would have been to turn right (to starboard) to pass well clear astern of ts1.

t=150s: own-ship cited Rule 14 (head-on) and turned right, but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because ts1 bore 98deg relative, CPA=0.101NM, TCPA=663s -- this is a fabricated citation. -- violates the principle that COLREG manoeuvring rules apply only when risk of collision exists (Rule 7); the COLREG-compliant action would have been to maintain course and speed, as no collision avoidance manoeuvre was required.

t=0s: own-ship cited Rule 13 (overtaking) and turned left, but the ground truth says Rule 15/Rule 16 applies (crossing encounter with target on starboard side) because ts1 bore 65deg relative, CPA=0.000NM, TCPA=386s -- this is a fabricated/incorrect citation. -- violates Rule 15 because as the give-way vessel in a crossing encounter with a target on own-ship's starboard side, own-ship must keep out of the way and should take early and substantial action to starboard, not turn to port; the COLREG-compliant action would have been to turn right (to starboard) to pass well clear astern of ts1.

t=150s: own-ship cited Rule 14 (head-on) and turned right, but the ground truth says no rule applies (quiet -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision) because ts1 bore 98deg relative, CPA=0.101NM, TCPA=663s -- this is a fabricated citation. -- violates the principle that COLREG manoeuvring rules apply only when risk of collision exists (Rule 7); the COLREG-compliant action would have been to maintain course and speed, as no collision avoidance manoeuvre was required.
compliant_actions: t=300s: own-ship cited Rule 15 (crossing) and turned left to port -- correctly satisfies Rule 15/Rule 16 in this specific context because the ground truth confirms a crossing encounter with ts1 on starboard (65deg → 70deg relative bearing, CPA=0.018NM, TCPA=168s), and by t=300s own-ship had already been on a port-turning trajectory for 150 seconds; continuing that established turn to open the CPA further was a reasonable continuation of the give-way vessel's obligation to keep out of the way, given the geometry and prior manoeuvring.

t=450s: own-ship cited Rule 15 (crossing) and turned left to port -- correctly satisfies Rule 15/Rule 16 in this specific context because the ground truth confirms a crossing encounter with ts1 on starboard (bearing 105deg relative, CPA=0.042NM, TCPA=74s), and own-ship's continued port turn was part of an ongoing manoeuvre to increase separation and pass clear of the target, fulfilling the give-way vessel's obligation to keep out of the way.

t=600s: own-ship cited Rule 13 (overtaking) and turned right to starboard -- correctly satisfies Rule 13 because the ground truth confirms ts1 was overtaking own-ship (bearing 164deg relative, CPA=0.050NM, TCPA=59s), and as the stand-on vessel being overtaken, own-ship is entitled to manoeuvre (Rule 13 imposes obligations on the overtaking vessel, not restrictions on the vessel being overtaken); turning to starboard to aid safe passage was appropriate.

t=750s: own-ship cited Rule 13 (overtaking) and turned right to starboard -- correctly satisfies Rule 13 because the ground truth confirms ts1 was overtaking own-ship (bearing -129deg relative, CPA=0.134NM, TCPA=0s at CPA), and own-ship's starboard turn as the vessel being overtaken was a permissible action to maintain or increase separation.

t=900s: own-ship cited no rule and turned right to starboard -- correctly satisfies the principle that when no collision risk exists, a vessel may manoeuvre freely for navigation purposes; the ground truth confirms no rule applies (ts1 bearing -137deg relative, CPA=0.363NM, TCPA=0s -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision).

t=1050s: own-ship cited no rule and turned right to starboard -- correctly satisfies the principle that when no collision risk exists, a vessel may manoeuvre freely for navigation purposes; the ground truth confirms no rule applies (ts1 bearing -154deg relative, CPA=0.667NM, TCPA=0s -- CPA/TCPA too large for real risk of collision).

params.system_prompt:
You are the navigator on a large commercial vessel. Decide the next helm order.

MISSION REQUIREMENTS -- this mission is only completed successfully if ALL of these hold, not just
the first one you happen to satisfy:
1. Every contact's CPA stays at or above this mission's safe passing distance (given further below)
   at all times -- exactly as mandatory as actually reaching the goal. There is no automatic safety
   net correcting your choice if you get this wrong: your own action each step is what the ship
   actually does.
2. Every manoeuvre you take while a real collision risk exists complies with COLREG.
3. You reach the mission goal.

PRIORITY ORDER when these pull in different directions -- always in this order, never reversed:
1. Collision avoidance: if any contact poses a real risk of collision, resolve it per COLREG first.
2. Mission progress: otherwise, move toward the mission goal as directly and efficiently as possible.

FACTS GIVEN TO YOU -- treat all of these as already correct; never recompute, re-derive, or
second-guess them:
- Positions/bearings/headings are in metres/degrees, heading 0=north, clockwise (compass convention).
- rel.bearing is signed: positive=starboard (right), negative=port (left), 0=dead ahead, ~180/-180=astern.
- CPA = the closest distance a contact will EVER come to you at current headings/speeds. TCPA = seconds
  until that closest point.
- TCPA=0 does NOT always mean an imminent collision -- it also happens once the closest point has
  already passed (the situation report says so explicitly when that's the case). Judge real risk from
  CPA alone, never from TCPA alone.
- The situation report's "GOAL COURSE CHECK:" line has ALREADY computed the goal-correction action and
  degrees for you. Never substitute a contact's rel.bearing for it -- that number describes the
  CONTACT, not the goal, even when the numbers look similar.

DECISION PROCEDURE -- follow in order:
1. Check every contact's CPA against this mission's safe passing distance (given further below). If
   none are below it, there is no real collision risk right now -- go to step 3.
2. If any contact's CPA is below the safe passing distance, pick the ONE action that satisfies the
   applicable COLREG rule for that contact. This step overrides everything below it.
3. Otherwise, follow "GOAL COURSE CHECK" exactly: hold_course if it says you're already on the goal
   bearing, or copy its exact action and degrees if it names a turn -- do not recompute or replace
   those values.
4. Never zigzag: do not answer turn_right then turn_left (or vice versa) on consecutive decisions to
   chase a small residual mismatch -- "GOAL COURSE CHECK" already has a deadband built in for this.
5. If you are already on the goal bearing and your speed is below this mission's nominal/rated speed,
   speed_up instead of hold_course -- reaching the goal sooner (when safe) is also progress.

Ground your reasoning in the COLREG excerpts/procedure guidance provided, where given. Reply with
ONLY a JSON object, no other text:
{"action": "turn_left|turn_right|hold_course|speed_up|slow_down|stop",
 "degrees": <float, only for turn_left/turn_right>,
 "rule_applied": "<e.g. Rule 15, or 'none' if no rule applies>",
 "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"}
